publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Characterisation of Oscillators Design and Measurement
IEE Colloquium on Characterisation of Oscillators Design and Measurement
abstract: A novel tuneable quasi-optical scheme is presented to provide stabilisation of both fundamental and second-harmonic oscillators at W-band, with excellent isolation from the load. A decrease in phase noise by more than 4dB on free-running Gunn oscillators at 90 GHz is demonstrated with SSB phase noise better than -120 dBc/Hz at 100 kHz away from the carrier. This is believed to be state of the art.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Characterisation of Oscillators Design and Measurement
abstract: The design and performance of tuned bipolar transistor power oscillators is presented. An efficiency of 54% was obtained with an output power of 26 dBm at 800 MHz and a noise level of -80 dBc/Hz at 10 kHz offset. The design method is an improved version of Kazimierczuk's procedure.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Characterisation of Oscillators Design and Measurement
abstract: The aim of this work was an investigation of the GaAs heterojunction bipolar transistor (HBT) for wide tuning range, low phase noise oscillators including, for the first time, a YIG-tuned HBT oscillator. The article describes two types of electronically tuned oscillators, firstly ones based on varactor tuning and secondly a YIG tuned type. Varactor tuned oscillators (VTO) offer high tuning rates and low power consumption in a small, light-weight package. Whilst tuning ranges are adequate for many applications, they are smaller than can be obtained with a YTO. The limited Q of wide capacitance range varactor diodes degrades the phase noise of VTOs. By comparison the YIG-tuned oscillator (YTO) has a very wide tuning range (though not such high tuning rates as a VTO) with good linearity and excellent phase noise performance. This paper will give results on these two types of oscillator and compare them with similar circuits built using GaAs FETs or silicon BJTs.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Quasi-optical millimetre wave oscillator & power combiner
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Characterisation of Oscillators Design and Measurement
abstract: The present interest in quasi-optical resonators is for CW and pulse power combining at short millimetric wavelengths where, owing to the highly overmoded cavity geometry, arrays of discrete gain elements may be accommodated on the mirror surfaces and the output powers combined in a single cavity mode. In order to accommodate significant numbers of source modules alternative resonator geometries utilising corner reflectors are also under investigation. The advantages of this arrangement are three-fold: (a) The roof reflector provides a greater surface area for supporting the active array (b) The resonator symmetry can now be maintained by using two spherical mirrors (c) More sophisticated output coupling arrangements can be employed as the end mirror is no longer required to support the array.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: High power vacuum tube oscillator design
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Characterisation of Oscillators Design and Measurement
abstract: By making changes in the feedback circuit and compensating adjustments to the anode load, it should be possible to make an oscillator work with constant DC voltages and currents but with a wide variation in efficiency. As the efficiency is reduced it would be expected that the RF anode swing would increase. To test this the experiments described were done.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A high spectral purity reference standard for the phase noise characterisation of microwave sources
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Characterisation of Oscillators Design and Measurement
abstract: Describes an X-band discriminator stabilised solid state microwave source with close to carrier phase noise around 15 dB lower than that obtainable from crystal multiplier or phase locked sources. The design is such that the performance achieved is highly repeatable, making the source suitable for use as a reference standard in phase noise measurement.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Direct digital synthesis phase noise properties
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Characterisation of Oscillators Design and Measurement
abstract: Reports the phase noise characteristics of a 100 MHz ECL direct digital synthesiser that produces a close to carrier phase noise profile comparable to the very best oscillators, e.g. -120 dBc/Hz at 10 Hz offset from a 5.85 MHz carrier. In addition, from the measured results, a relationship is established between the phase noise profile of the synthesised waveform and the phase noise profile of the clock source used.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The characteristics of a class of pulsed quartz oscillators
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Characterisation of Oscillators Design and Measurement
abstract: Chemically etched and plasma etched 'VHF' quartz crystals potentially offer the RF designer a significant advantage over conventional quartz crystals when employed in oscillator configurations. Instead of obtaining a stable VHF or UHF frequency source by multiplication and filtering, oscillation is possible directly at the wanted frequency. For the systems designer this can mean fewer or possibly no frequency multiplication stages to obtain a stable VHF/UHF frequency. Because of low spurious outputs the advantages may well prove significant in the overall RF systems performance. Two potential advantages are the elimination of multiplicative frequency drift and phase noise of the oscillator which increases by (20log*(multiplication factor)). A real bonus is that harmonic filtering requirements become less critical or indeed filters may be eliminated altogether. In the application considered here, this is an important point because the unavoidable additional loss resulting from filters and the increased component count can be very significant and to be avoided if at all possible, hence the potential attractiveness of 'VHF' crystals.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An RFOW testable DRO for use within a complete MMIC low noise downconverter
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Characterisation of Oscillators Design and Measurement
abstract: Describes the design of an RF-on-wafer (RFOW) testable MMIC-based dielectric resonator oscillator (DRO) utilised within a single chip MMIC DBS low noise downconverter (LNC). The LNC is required to cover the RF band of 10.95-12.7 GHz, with IF output in the range 0.95-1.7 GHz. The DRO local oscillator (LO) is purposely designed to cover a wider band than the necessary 10-11 GHz to allow downconverter operation over a wider range, albeit with reduced performance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
